config.title: aspect-ratio

intro.title: aspect-ratio
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple responsive image gallery where each image maintains a consistent shape regardless of its size. You will learn the core CSS concept of the aspect-ratio property, which allows you to control the width-to-height ratio of an element. The main technology involved is CSS, using the aspect-ratio property to ensure elements scale proportionally. This beginner-friendly lesson will help you create visually balanced layouts that adapt smoothly to different screen sizes.
intro.usecase: The aspect-ratio property is essential for creating responsive media containers that maintain their proportions across different screen sizes. Developers use it to ensure images, videos, and embedded content like YouTube players don't distort when containers resize. This is particularly valuable in product galleries, social media feeds, and dashboard widgets where consistent visual presentation matters. By using aspect-ratio, you can create fluid layouts that adapt to various devices while preserving intended design aesthetics.

objectives: Apply the aspect-ratio property to maintain proportional dimensions of an element.
Configure aspect-ratio values for common shapes like squares and widescreen rectangles.
Manipulate aspect-ratio to control responsive behavior across viewport sizes.
Integrate aspect-ratio with other CSS properties like width or max-width for flexible layouts.
Construct a media container that preserves its intended proportions without manual height calculations.
Update existing CSS rules to replace fixed height declarations with dynamic aspect-ratio.
Initialize aspect-ratio on images and videos to prevent layout shifts during loading.

steps.title: Create a container element for aspect-ratio examples
steps.instruction: Create a div element with class 'container' in your HTML file to serve as the parent container for aspect-ratio examples.
steps.hint: Start with a simple div element and give it a class attribute with the value 'container'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A div element with class 'container' is created in your HTML file.
successCriteria: The HTML contains a div element with class attribute set to 'container'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a div element with class='container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create a div element with class='container' in your HTML.

steps.title: Add a basic box element to demonstrate default behavior
steps.instruction: Inside the existing container element, add a new div element with the class name 'box'.
steps.hint: Add a child div element with class="box" inside the container div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML structure will have a container with a nested box element.
successCriteria: A div with class 'box' exists as a child of the container div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an element, but make sure it's a div with exactly class='box' and it's placed inside the container div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The box element isn't properly added. Check that you have a div with class='box' nested inside the container div.

steps.title: Style the box with basic dimensions and background
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules for the .box class to set its width to 200px, height to 150px, and background-color to lightblue.
steps.hint: Use the .box selector in your CSS and define the width, height, and background-color properties with the specified values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will become a visible rectangle with light blue background, 200px wide and 150px tall.
successCriteria: The .box class has width: 200px, height: 150px, and background-color: lightblue defined in the CSS.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've included all three properties: width, height, and background-color with the correct values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS for .box doesn't match the required styling. Make sure to add width: 200px, height: 150px, and background-color: lightblue.

steps.title: Add a second box element for aspect-ratio comparison
steps.instruction: Add another div element with class 'box aspect-box' inside the container div, right after the existing box.
steps.hint: Copy the existing box div and add the additional 'aspect-box' class to it.
steps.analogousExample: /* Adding a second element for comparison */
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML structure now contains two box elements inside the container, with the second one having both 'box' and 'aspect-box' classes.
successCriteria: A second div element with class 'box aspect-box' is present inside the container div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a second div element with both 'box' and 'aspect-box' classes inside the container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second box element with class 'box aspect-box' is missing from the container. Check that you've added it correctly.

steps.title: Apply the aspect-ratio property to the second box
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a new class named '.aspect-box' that sets aspect-ratio: 1/1.
steps.hint: Create a new CSS selector that targets the class 'aspect-box' and apply the aspect-ratio property with a value of 1/1.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for the class 'aspect-box' is created with the aspect-ratio property set to a 1:1 ratio.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a rule for '.aspect-box' with 'aspect-ratio: 1/1;'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a CSS rule for '.aspect-box', but the aspect-ratio value might be missing or incorrect. Ensure it's set to '1/1'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for '.aspect-box' with aspect-ratio: 1/1 is not present. Please add it as instructed.

steps.title: Remove fixed height from the aspect-ratio box
steps.instruction: In the .aspect-box CSS rule, remove the height property while keeping the width property to see how aspect-ratio works with only one dimension defined.
steps.hint: Delete the line that sets height on .aspect-box, but leave the width property intact.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .aspect-box CSS rule should have width defined but no height property, allowing aspect-ratio to control the height automatically.
successCriteria: The .aspect-box CSS rule contains width but not height, while aspect-ratio is present.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've removed the height property from .aspect-box while keeping the width property.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your .aspect-box CSS rule. It should have width defined but no height property.

steps.title: Create a rectangle element with different aspect ratio
steps.instruction: Add a new div element with class 'rectangle' inside the container, after the existing boxes.
steps.hint: Place the new div element between the closing tag of .aspect-box and the closing tag of .container.

steps.expectedOutcome: A new div element with class 'rectangle' appears in the HTML structure, ready for styling.
successCriteria: The HTML contains a div element with class='rectangle' inside the container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a div element with class='rectangle' inside the container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The rectangle element is missing. Add a div with class='rectangle' inside the container.

steps.title: Add responsive behavior to the rectangle
steps.instruction: Make the aspect-ratio box responsive by setting its width to 50% of the container.
steps.hint: Add a width property to the .aspect-box selector in your CSS.
steps.expectedOutcome: The aspect-ratio box will now be responsive, taking up half the container width while maintaining its square shape.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added width: 50%; to the .aspect-box selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The aspect-ratio box should have width: 50%; to make it responsive. Check the .aspect-box selector in your CSS.

steps.title: Create an element with max-width constraint
steps.instruction: Add a new div element with class 'constrained' inside the container, after the existing boxes.
steps.hint: Add a new <div> tag with class="constrained" between the closing tag of .aspect-box and the closing tag of .container.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new empty div element with class 'constrained' appears in the container after the aspect-box.
successCriteria: A div element with class='constrained' is added inside the container element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an element, but make sure it has exactly class='constrained' and is placed inside the container after the aspect-box.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constrained element wasn't added correctly. Check that you're adding a div with class='constrained' inside the container.
